subject: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@pulsecare.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

Hi Morgan / Anika —

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. Attached is our initial runbook (streaming-toolcall-runbook-v1.pdf) and the first draft JSON schema (pulsecare-schema-draft.json). This is meant to be an actionable checklist we can follow for the feature enablement so your engineers can start calling the streaming endpoint, use function/tool-calls, and validate structured outputs.

Top-level asks from Redwood for the first pass:
- Align on the JSON schema fields (we've marked optional vs required).
- Confirm which PulseCare service will serve as the primary tool invocation target (e.g., patient-lookup or billing-ops).
- Provide sample payloads for 3 representative flows (clinical note ingestion, billing lookup, and appointment search).

Proposed near-term milestones (we can adjust in our shared doc):
1) Schema sync + sample payloads — due Mon 2026-03-09
2) Implementation call (streaming + tool-call flows) — Wed 2026-03-11 11:00 PST
3) Canary rollout (48h) + monitoring hooks — week of 2026-03-16

Can you confirm the implementation call time and who from your engineering team will join? I copied the internal owners above: Dylan will drive schema work, Connor will handle SDK/integration guidance, and Laura will own observability and alerting runbooks.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: streaming-toolcall-runbook-v1.pdf (13 pages), pulsecare-schema-draft.json (6 KB)

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@pulsecare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Patel <anika.p@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

On Mon, Mar 8, 2026 at 09:15 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the kickoff yesterday...

Thanks Monica — the runbook looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
1) On the JSON schema draft, can you confirm whether timestamps should be RFC3339? Our backend currently uses epoch ms in some places and RFC3339 in others.
2) For function/tool-calls, will Redwood require an additional API key with narrower scopes for the tool invocation (we're trying to avoid giving broad service credentials)?

We can join Wed 3/11 for the implementation call. I'll ask our lead engineer (Anika) to attend. Also attaching a short payload export from our staging environment that might help — will follow up with a cleaned CSV after a quick scrub.

—Morgan
Morgan Lee
Head of Integrations, PulseCare
Attachment stub: pulsecare-staging-export.csv (truncated)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@pulsecare.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

Morgan — thanks, and great questions. Short answers: 
- Use RFC3339 timestamps in the schema (we recommend ISO 8601 / RFC3339 for consistent parsing in streaming contexts). We'll mark the schema draft accordingly.
- For tool-calls we support per-integration scoped API keys. Connor will share the recommended least-privilege manifest we prefer (example below).

Example least-privilege manifest (manifest.json snippet):
{
  "integration": "pulsecare-patient-lookup",
  "scopes": ["read:patients","invoke:patient-lookup"],
  "allowed_ips": ["*"],
  "token_ttl_minutes": 60
}

Connor will attach a runnable SDK snippet during the call. For streaming, the main gotchas are: keep your chunk sizes under 4k tokens for consistent latency, implement prefix caching for repeated patient identifiers, and ensure your ingress path supports HTTP/2.

I've updated the Google doc with the RFC3339 change: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBC_runbook_pulsecare (see Schema section).

See you on Wednesday.
—Monica

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

I'll take the schema finalization. Monica — can you ask PulseCare to provide 3 sample payloads in the following form (CSV or JSONL): flow_type, record_count, example_payload (JSON escaped). That will let me create fixture-based unit tests and a JSON Schema with concrete examples.

Connor — once I have sample payloads I will produce a strict schema + a permissive compatibility mode for their existing staging data.

Attachment: pulsecare-sample-payloads.csv (stub)

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@pulsecare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Patel <anika.p@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

Thanks Dylan — attaching the cleaned sample payloads (pulsecare-sample-payloads.csv). A couple notes: we standardized timestamps to RFC3339 and added an event_type field. Also, we'd like a canary rollout plan that keeps the legacy path for any records missing the new event_type. Is there a standard Redwood pattern for that?

On the canary: we'd prefer a 48-hour canary with 10% traffic, then a 1-week ramp to 100% if there are no regressions. Can you add monitoring checks for structured output validation failures and spike in latency?

—Morgan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@pulsecare.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PulseCare: Feature rollout runbook for streaming, tool-calls, and JSON schema

Morgan/Anika — great, thanks for the sample payloads and for standardizing timestamps. We've updated the runbook and attached the rollout timeline (rollout-timeline-canary.xlsx). Summary of changes and next steps: 

- Schema: RFC3339 timestamps required; event_type added (string enum: ["clinical_note","billing_lookup","appointment_search"]). Dylan to hand over final schema by end of day 2026-03-12.
- Tool-calls: We'll use per-integration scoped API keys and Connor will share the least-privilege manifest and a short Node/Python SDK snippet on the call.
- Streaming: Follow chunking guidance; implement prefix caching for patient identifiers.
- Canary plan: 48h at 10% -> 3 days at 35% -> 1 week full ramp contingent on zero structured-output failures and <10% latency increase. Laura will provision the monitoring dashboard and alert rule IDs this week.
- Owners: Dylan (schema/tests), Connor (SDK/integration examples), Laura (observability), Monica (project lead / escalation).

Please confirm the Wed 3/11 11:00 PST implementation call (we have it on our calendars). If that works, Connor will drop the SDK snippet and I will screen-share the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to the rollout.
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: rollout-timeline-canary.xlsx (6 KB)
